  PROBLEM: A marker with `pending: true` for a switch that is not on the default branch yet logs the "off_on_purpose marker for unknown switch ... ignored" warning on every daily run until its pull request merges. This is documented behaviour, but it is noise.
  WHY: The registry test accepts this state on purpose. Suggested minimal fix: skip the warning (still ignore the marker) when `marker.get("pending") is True` and the name is not in the merged list. Estimated lines changed: 2. HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1.

The reviewer proposes either adding the file to the plan and removing the field (~175 mechanical edits), or re-stating G2 in the README/agents fragment. It argues that G4 forbids text edits, not the deletion of a redundant field. It also notes that the pass-1 editor's rejection was reasonable.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3

  File: tests/test_stage_switch_watch.py
  Line or code reference: `test_invalid_marker_pending_exits_2` (newly added in last run)
  Requirement: The test only covers a marker whose `name` (`ALPHA_ENABLED`) is also listed in `switches`. A marker with an undiscovered `name` and a non-boolean `pending` is not tested.

  SEVERITY: NIT
